summary: No reachable vulnerabilities. Untrusted input is the stored settings record (editable in devtools). readSettings validates it with parseSettings, which is strict (object type, enum defaultSpeed, five typeof-boolean checks) and returns a fresh copy with only the known fields, so extra or hostile keys are dropped. It throws inside an async function, so the promise rejects, and App's launch effect catches that and falls back to DEFAULT_SETTINGS. The Settings checkbox then becomes enabled, and the next toggle overwrites the bad record with a valid one. Nothing is left stuck. writeSettings also runs parseSettings before put(), so a bad record is never written. Any rejection (validation or IDB) is caught and logged in changeSettings, and the UI state is already updated. The label is static React text with no HTML sink. There are no new dependencies, secrets, network calls or randomness.
